subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-profile pool-routing config/API, or keep this work to narrower auth-profile rotation, quota/bucket cooldown, and provider/probe fixes for now?
rationale: Source inspection shows a real missing capability, but the requested solution would define public config, persisted state, fallback behavior, and session stickiness semantics that automation should not invent without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design additive core pool routing
options.body: Sponsor a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract with explicit defaults, one initial strategy, status/probe observability, and upgrade-safe config handling.

options.title: Phase narrower routing fixes
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker while solving quota buckets, same-provider retry depth, and model/auth binding in separate narrower issues first.

options.title: Defer to sidecar or plugin exploration
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged until an external prototype proves the missing plugin/API seam and the native surface is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design additive core pool routing
recommendation.body: Sponsor a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract with explicit defaults, one initial strategy, status/probe observability, and upgrade-safe config handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is product/config direction across auth, provider routing, fallback, and session behavior, and this person has the strongest historical signal on those boundaries among the identified owners.
